subject: Request: Cross-year Anchor + Stepdown Exception for AtlasHealth (DEAL-87421)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@atlashealth.com>, Meera Patel <meera.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial pricing proposal and cross-year anchor ask (DEAL-87421)

Sanjay / Meera —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is the pricing summary for AtlasHealth's three-year plan. A couple of key asks from your side I want to summarize so we have alignment before we loop Deal Desk:

- Cross-year anchor: Atlas asked that the base unit price be locked for the first 24 months, with a capped step-up in year 3 (no more than +8% year-over-year).
- Early-year consumption rebate tied to committed throughput (details in attachment).
- Renewal protection: if Atlas expands in years 1–2, the expanded units should be grandfathered at an intermediate band for 12 months.

We're supportive of a long-term partnership and want to be flexible, but this request is outside standard deal desk guardrails. Marcus / Marissa — copying you to start an internal thread for an exception.

Attachment: 2028-07-20_Atlas_pricing_summary.pdf (pdf, 225KB)

Next steps I propose: internal review -> Deal Desk exception -> legal redline for the MSA.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Office: +1 415 555 0147
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@atlashealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Patel <meera.patel@atlashealth.com>, AtlasHealth Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing proposal and cross-year anchor ask (DEAL-87421)

Laura —

Thanks for the summary and quick turnaround. A couple clarifications:

1) The 24-month lock is critical for our board — we need predictable unit economics as we model product launches for 2029.
2) The +8% cap in year 3 is a hard requirement; anything above that is a non-starter.
3) We will sign an expanded commitment addendum if Redwood agrees to the anchor + 12-month grandfather on expansions.

Legal will review the MSA changes once you provide them.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement, AtlasHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas pricing request — initial assessment

Folks — forwarding the Atlas request. Quick assessment below:

- Cross-year anchor (24 months): high commercial value — reduces churn risk and drives predictable committed revenue.
- Year-3 step-up cap at +8%: moderately aggressive relative to our standard 10–12% uplifts; 8% is close but tighter than guardrails.
- Expansion grandfathering for 12 months: increases expansion smoothing risk (hard to reprice) but reasonable if we add volume-based escape clauses.

Requesting: Deal Desk exception to allow a 24-month lock with a maximum +8% in year 3 and a 12-month expansion grandfather, contingent on: (1) minimum 18-month committed spend floor, and (2) legal-approved addendum with explicit volume escape triggers.

Attachment: None

Please reply with fast-track or escalate to Marissa for exec signoff.

-Marcus
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Atlas pricing request — Deal Desk exception assessment

Marcus / team —

I reviewed the numbers and modeled three scenarios (conservative / base / upside). Key points:

- Required protection: if we give a 24-month price lock, we need a minimum committed spend equal to ~60% of projected run-rate for months 1–18. This protects us against small, high-discount pilots.
- Escape triggers: automatic repricing if monthly consumption falls below 70% of the committed run-rate for any continuous 90-day window.
- Year-3 cap: 8% is acceptable provided we have a stepdown floor for downgrades and a 12-month grandfather for expansions (as Marcus suggested).

I've attached a redline of the MSA with the proposed addendum language for legal review. If Marissa signs off, I recommend offering Atlas a 24-month lock + 8% year-3 cap, conditional on: 18-month minimum spend floor + 90-day consumption escape clause + signed addendum.

Attachment: 2028-07-21_ATLAS_redlined_MSA.docx (docx, 48KB)

-Aditya Rao
